source.text: וְלִבְנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן מַחְלְקוֹתָ֑ם בְּנֵ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן נָדָב֙ וַאֲבִיה֔וּא אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וְאִיתָמָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And to [the] sons of Aaron, their divisions: [the] sons of Aaron [were] Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

en.L: And of the sons of Aaron, their divisions: the sons of Aaron [were] Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
en.B: The descendants of Aaron were grouped in divisions as follows. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
en.R: Here are the groups that Aaron's descendants were divided into. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

decisions.choice: divisions: groups that took turns serving
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "divide" used in verses 3-5. It names the groups the priests were split into, each serving at the sanctuary in its turn (verse 19). The same word was used for the Levites' groups in 23:6.

decisions.choice: as for the sons of Aaron: a heading, then the four sons
decisions.reason: The opening "to the sons of Aaron" introduces a new list, as 23:6 did for the Levites. The first "sons of Aaron" means the whole priestly family descended from him; the second means his four actual sons.

decisions.choice: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar: Aaron's four sons
decisions.reason: The same four names are given in Exodus 6:23 and Numbers 3:2.

decisions.choice: descendants (first); sons (second)
decisions.reason: The two uses of "sons" mean different things (m2), so Balanced and Readable say "descendants" for the whole family and keep "sons" for Aaron's own children.

source.text: וַיָּ֨מָת נָדָ֤ב וַאֲבִיהוּא֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֲבִיהֶ֔ם וּבָנִ֖ים לֹא־הָי֣וּ לָהֶ֑ם וַֽיְכַהֲנ֔וּ אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וְאִיתָמָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And died Nadab and Abihu before their father, and sons not were to them; and served as priests Eleazar and Ithamar.

en.L: And Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and they had no sons; and Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
en.B: But Nadab and Abihu died in their father's lifetime, leaving no sons, and Eleazar and Ithamar served as the priests.
en.R: But Nadab and Abihu died while their father was still alive, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar were the ones who served as priests.

decisions.choice: the death of Nadab and Abihu told in Leviticus 10:1-2
decisions.reason: Leviticus 10:1-2 tells how Nadab and Abihu offered fire the LORD had not commanded and were killed by fire from the LORD. Numbers 3:4 adds that they had no sons, as this verse does. Chronicles names their death without retelling its cause.

decisions.choice: before their father: while Aaron was still living
decisions.reason: "Before the face of their father" can mean in his sight, and Aaron was present when they died (Leviticus 10:3). Here the point is time: they died before him and left no heirs. Numbers 3:4 uses a similar phrase for Eleazar and Ithamar serving during Aaron's lifetime.

decisions.choice: no sons: no priestly line came from Nadab and Abihu
decisions.reason: Because they left no descendants, every priestly division in this chapter comes from Eleazar or Ithamar (verse 4).

decisions.choice: in their father's lifetime; while their father was still alive; were the ones who
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the time sense of m2 plain, and Readable spells out the result of m3 for young readers.

source.text: וַיֶּֽחָלְקֵ֣ם דָּוִ֔יד וְצָדוֹק֙ מִן־בְּנֵ֣י אֶלְעָזָ֔ר וַאֲחִימֶ֖לֶךְ מִן־בְּנֵ֣י אִיתָמָ֑ר לִפְקֻדָּתָ֖ם בַּעֲבֹדָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And divided them David, and Zadok from [the] sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech from [the] sons of Ithamar, according to their appointment in their service.

en.L: And David divided them, with Zadok from the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech from the sons of Ithamar, according to their appointment in their service.
en.B: With the help of Zadok, a descendant of Eleazar, and Ahimelech, a descendant of Ithamar, David divided them into their appointed order for their service.
en.R: David divided the priests into groups so that each group would have its turn to serve. Zadok, from Eleazar's family, and Ahimelech, from Ithamar's family, helped him.

decisions.choice: David is the one who acts; Zadok and Ahimelech join him
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, "he divided", with David as its subject and Zadok and Ahimelech added after him. David makes the arrangement, and the two priests take part, each for his own branch of Aaron's family.

decisions.choice: Zadok and Ahimelech: the heads of the two priestly lines
decisions.reason: Zadok came from Eleazar (5:30-34). Ahimelech was the son of Abiathar (verse 6), the priest who escaped Saul's killing of the priests at Nob and served David (1 Samuel 22:20; 2 Samuel 8:17). Here he stands for Ithamar's line.

decisions.choice: appointment: the office and turn of duty assigned to each group
decisions.reason: The noun means something assigned or put in charge. With "their service" it names the duty each group held and the time it served, as verse 19 shows.

decisions.choice: With the help of Zadok ... and Ahimelech ..., David divided them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the roles of m1 in natural English: David acts, and the two priests help. Readable also names "the priests" as the ones divided.

source.text: וַיִּמָּצְא֣וּ בְֽנֵי־אֶלְעָזָ֡ר רַבִּ֞ים לְרָאשֵׁ֧י הַגְּבָרִ֛ים מִן־בְּנֵ֥י אִיתָמָ֖ר וַֽיַּחְלְק֑וּם לִבְנֵ֨י אֶלְעָזָ֜ר רָאשִׁ֤ים לְבֵית־אָבוֹת֙ שִׁשָּׁ֣ה עָשָׂ֔ר וְלִבְנֵ֧י אִיתָמָ֛ר לְבֵ֥ית אֲבוֹתָ֖ם שְׁמוֹנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And were found [the] sons of Eleazar more as heads of the men than [the] sons of Ithamar, and they divided them: to [the] sons of Eleazar, heads of house of fathers, sixteen, and to [the] sons of Ithamar, by house of their fathers, eight.

en.L: And the sons of Eleazar were found [to be] more in chief men than the sons of Ithamar, and they divided them: for the sons of Eleazar, sixteen heads of fathers' houses, and for the sons of Ithamar, by their fathers' houses, eight.
en.B: Eleazar's descendants were found to have more leading men than Ithamar's, so they divided them this way: sixteen heads of ancestral families from Eleazar's descendants, and eight ancestral families from Ithamar's.
en.R: There were more leaders among Eleazar's descendants than among Ithamar's. So they made sixteen groups from the family leaders of Eleazar's line and eight from Ithamar's.

decisions.choice: fathers' houses: ancestral families, each under its own head
decisions.reason: A "father's house" was a family group descended from one ancestor and led by its head. Each such family became one of the priestly divisions.

decisions.choice: sixteen and eight: the twenty-four divisions
decisions.reason: Sixteen and eight make the twenty-four divisions whose lots are listed in verses 7-18. Each line received divisions in proportion to the number of its leading men.

decisions.choice: ancestral families (Balanced); family leaders, groups (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Fathers' houses" is kept at Literal. Balanced says "ancestral families" and Readable "families", as the other chapters do; Readable adds "groups" to link these families to the divisions.

source.text: וַיַּחְלְק֥וּם בְּגוֹרָל֖וֹת אֵ֣לֶּה עִם־אֵ֑לֶּה כִּי־הָי֤וּ שָֽׂרֵי־קֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ וְשָׂרֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים מִבְּנֵ֥י אֶלְעָזָ֖ר וּבִבְנֵ֥י אִיתָמָֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they divided them by lots, these with these, for were princes of holiness and princes of the God from [the] sons of Eleazar and among [the] sons of Ithamar.

en.L: And they divided them by lots, these with these, for there were princes of holiness and princes of God from the sons of Eleazar and among the sons of Ithamar.
en.B: They divided them by lot, one group the same as the other, because there were officials of the sanctuary and officials of God among the descendants of Eleazar and among the descendants of Ithamar.
en.R: They used lots to divide both families in the same way, because both Eleazar's and Ithamar's descendants included leaders in the holy place and leaders in God's service.

decisions.choice: these with these: both lines treated alike
decisions.reason: "These with these" means the lots were cast for both lines together, with no preference. The lot, not rank or family, decided the order (Proverbs 16:33; 18:18).

decisions.choice: officials of the sanctuary and officials of God: men of high standing in the priesthood
alternatives: two titles for the same men, the leaders of the priesthood
two different ranks: some over the sanctuary, others over the matters of God
decisions.reason: These two titles appear together nowhere else ("princes of holiness" also occurs at Isaiah 43:28), and "holiness" may mean the holy place. They may be two names for the same leading priests, or two different ranks, one over the sanctuary and one over the matters of God (compare 2 Chronicles 19:11). Either way the point is clear: both lines had leading men, so the order was left to the lot.

decisions.choice: for: the reason lots were used
decisions.reason: Because both lines had men of equal standing, their order of service could not fairly be set by rank.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "princes" for this word as elsewhere. Balanced says "officials" and Readable "leaders", as for this word elsewhere in these books. Readable explains "of holiness" and "of God" as "in the holy place" and "in God's service".

source.text: וַֽיִּכְתְּבֵ֡ם שְֽׁמַֽעְיָה֩ בֶן־נְתַנְאֵ֨ל הַסּוֹפֵ֜ר מִן־הַלֵּוִ֗י לִפְנֵ֨י הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִים֙ וְצָד֣וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וַאֲחִימֶ֨לֶךְ֙ בֶּן־אֶבְיָתָ֔ר וְרָאשֵׁי֙ הָֽאָב֔וֹת לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֑ם בֵּֽית־אָ֣ב אֶחָ֗ד אָחֻז֙ לְאֶלְעָזָ֔ר וְאָחֻ֥ז׀אָחֻ֖ז לְאִיתָמָֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And recorded them Shemaiah son of Nethanel the scribe, from the Levite[s], before the king and the princes and Zadok the priest and Ahimelech son of Abiathar and [the] heads of the fathers of the priests and of the Levites; house of father one taken for Eleazar, and taken taken for Ithamar.

en.L: And Shemaiah son of Nethanel the scribe, of the Levites, recorded them before the king and the princes, and Zadok the priest and Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of the fathers' [houses] of the priests and of the Levites: one father's house being taken for Eleazar, and taken, taken for Ithamar.
en.B: Shemaiah son of Nethanel, the scribe, a Levite, recorded them in the presence of the king and the officials, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of the priestly and Levite families. One ancestral family was drawn for Eleazar, and one drawn for Ithamar.
en.R: Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a Levite who was a scribe, wrote down the names. The king, his leaders, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the leaders of the families of priests and Levites were all there as witnesses. Each time a family was chosen, it was for either Eleazar's line or Ithamar's line.

decisions.choice: the scribe recorded the lots before witnesses
decisions.reason: A scribe was an official who kept written records. The order was written down in front of the king, the priests and the family heads, so that it was fixed and could not be disputed later.

decisions.choice: one family drawn for Eleazar, and one drawn for Ithamar
alternatives: one for Eleazar, then one for Ithamar, alternately
families drawn for Eleazar and, likewise, for Ithamar, in no fixed pattern
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "one father's house taken for Eleazar, and taken, taken for Ithamar". The repeated "taken" is hard to explain. It may be a copying slip for "one taken", which gives a simple pattern of one family for each line in turn; or the doubling may stress that families were drawn for Ithamar too, one after another. The sense that both lines took part in one drawing is clear; the exact pattern is not.

decisions.choice: Ahimelech son of Abiathar: the priest of verse 3
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 18:16 spells his name Abimelech; 2 Samuel 8:17 has Ahimelech son of Abiathar, as here.

decisions.choice: officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: This word for the king's chief men is "princes" at Literal, "officials" at Balanced and "leaders" at Readable, as in the other chapters.

decisions.choice: were all there as witnesses
decisions.reason: "Before" these men means the writing was done in their presence; Readable says why their presence mattered (m1).

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַגּוֹרָ֤ל הָרִאשׁוֹן֙ לִיה֣וֹיָרִ֔יב לִֽידַעְיָ֖ה הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out the lot the first to Jehoiarib, to Jedaiah the second,

en.L: And the first lot went out to Jehoiarib, to Jedaiah the second,
en.B: The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
en.R: The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, and the second to Jedaiah.

decisions.choice: the lot went out: the lot was drawn
decisions.reason: Lots were drawn or shaken out of a container, and the one that "went out" named whose turn it was (Joshua 19:1).

decisions.choice: one list from verse 7 to verse 18
decisions.reason: Verses 7-18 are one sentence: each name receives the lot of the number given with it. Each name is the head of a family, and later divisions kept these names (9:10; Nehemiah 12:1-7 lists several of them).

decisions.choice: one formula kept for all twenty-four lots
decisions.reason: Literal follows the Hebrew order ("to Jedaiah the second"). Balanced puts the number first ("the second to Jedaiah") and Readable uses short sentences ("The third lot fell to Harim, and the fourth to Seorim"). Each level keeps its formula unchanged through verse 18, and the lots for the singers in 25:9-31 use the same wording at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.reason: Luke 1:5 says the priest Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, belonged to the division of Abijah, the eighth division named here.

en.B: the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
en.R: The eleventh lot fell to Eliashib, and the twelfth to Jakim.

decisions.choice: eleven, twelve: used as "eleventh", "twelfth"
decisions.reason: Hebrew has separate words for "first" to "tenth" only. From eleven on, the plain number does the work of an ordinal, so "to Eliashib eleven" means the eleventh lot. The same holds to verse 18.

decisions.reason: The Hebrew name begins with the word "the", so the name is given as Ha-Pizzez, as the data spells it.

decisions.reason: Here the number has the article, "the twenty", which marks it as an ordinal. Jehezkel is the same Hebrew name as Ezekiel, who was also a priest (Ezekiel 1:3).

en.B: the twenty-third to Delaiah, the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
en.R: The twenty-third lot fell to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.

decisions.choice: twenty-four lots in all
decisions.reason: The list ends at twenty-four, the sixteen and eight of verse 4. It does not say which divisions came from Eleazar and which from Ithamar.

source.text: אֵ֣לֶּה פְקֻדָּתָ֞ם לַעֲבֹדָתָ֗ם לָב֤וֹא לְבֵית־יְהוָה֙ כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד אַהֲרֹ֣ן אֲבִיהֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔הוּ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: These [were] their appointment for their service, to come to [the] house of Yahweh according to their ordinance by [the] hand of Aaron their father, as commanded him Yahweh God of Israel.

en.L: These [were] their appointment for their service, to come into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} according to their ordinance by the hand of Aaron their father, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Israel had commanded him.
en.B: This was their appointed order for their service when they came into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, following the rule given them through Aaron their ancestor, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
en.R: This was the order in which they took turns serving when they went into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They followed the rules that Aaron their ancestor had given them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, had commanded him.

decisions.choice: appointment for their service: the order of duty each division held
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 3: the duty assigned to each division and the turn in which it served.

decisions.choice: according to their rule by the hand of Aaron: the order laid down through Aaron
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means through someone. The rules for priestly service came to Israel through Aaron (Exodus 28-29; Numbers 18:1-7), and the new divisions carry on that order.

decisions.choice: commanded him: the LORD commanded Aaron
decisions.reason: "Him" is Aaron, the ancestor just named. The arrangement David made rests on what God had commanded Aaron.

decisions.choice: ancestor
decisions.reason: "Father" here means forefather, so Balanced and Readable say "ancestor"; Literal keeps "father".

source.text: וְלִבְנֵ֥י לֵוִ֖י הַנּוֹתָרִ֑ים לִבְנֵ֤י עַמְרָם֙ שֽׁוּבָאֵ֔ל לִבְנֵ֥י שׁוּבָאֵ֖ל יֶחְדְּיָֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to [the] sons of Levi the remaining: to [the] sons of Amram, Shubael; to [the] sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.

en.L: And of the sons of Levi who remained: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
en.B: As for the rest of the descendants of Levi: from the sons of Amram, Shubael; from the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
en.R: These were the other descendants of Levi. From Amram's descendants came Shubael, and from Shubael's descendants came Jehdeiah.

decisions.choice: the rest of the Levites: those who were not priests, as listed in 23:12-23
decisions.reason: Verses 20-30 go back over the Levite families of 23:12-23, the Levites who were not descended from Aaron, and for several of them add the head of the next generation.

decisions.choice: Shubael: the Shebuel of 23:16
decisions.reason: In 23:16 the same man is spelled Shebuel, a son of Gershom son of Moses, which makes him one of the descendants of Amram. Jehdeiah is named here for the first time.

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: "Sons" here means the whole tribe, so Balanced and Readable say "descendants" at the head of the list.

source.text: לִרְחַבְיָ֑הוּ לִבְנֵ֣י רְחַבְיָ֔הוּ הָרֹ֖אשׁ יִשִּׁיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: To Rehabiah: to [the] sons of Rehabiah, the head, Isshiah.

en.L: Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, the head [was] Isshiah.
en.B: From Rehabiah: from the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah was the chief.
en.R: From Rehabiah's descendants, Isshiah was the leader.

decisions.choice: Rehabiah: the grandson of Moses
decisions.reason: Rehabiah was the son of Eliezer son of Moses, and had many descendants (23:15-17).

decisions.choice: the head: the first or chief son
decisions.reason: "The head" can mean the firstborn or the leading man of the family; either way Isshiah heads Rehabiah's line.

source.text: לַיִּצְהָרִ֣י שְׁלֹמ֔וֹת לִבְנֵ֥י שְׁלֹמ֖וֹת יָֽחַת׃

records.literal_gloss: To the Izharite: Shelomoth; to [the] sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.

en.L: Of the Izharites, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
en.B: From the Izharites: Shelomoth; from the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
en.R: From the family of Izhar came Shelomoth, and from Shelomoth's descendants came Jahath.

decisions.choice: Shelomoth: the Shelomith of 23:18
decisions.reason: 23:18 names Izhar's son as Shelomith, a slightly different spelling of the same name. Jahath is added here.

source.text: וּבְנָ֖י יְרִיָּ֑הוּ אֲמַרְיָ֨הוּ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י יַחֲזִיאֵל֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י יְקַמְעָ֖ם הָרְבִיעִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons: Jeriah, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.

en.L: And the sons [of Hebron]: Jeriah [the first], Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.
en.B: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth.
en.R: Hebron's sons were Jeriah the oldest, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth.

decisions.choice: the sons of Hebron, with Jeriah the first
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here says only "and the sons: Jeriah", without naming the father or calling Jeriah "the first". The same list in 23:19 reads "the sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first", so these words seem to have dropped out in copying here, and the sense is taken from 23:19.

decisions.choice: of Hebron; the first
decisions.reason: The missing words are supplied from 23:19, in brackets at Literal. Readable says "the oldest" for "the first".

source.text: בְּנֵ֤י עֻזִּיאֵל֙ מִיכָ֔ה לִבְנֵ֥י מִיכָ֖ה שָׁמִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Uzziel: Micah; to [the] sons of Micah, Shamir.

en.L: The sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir.
en.B: The sons of Uzziel: Micah; from the sons of Micah, Shamir.
en.R: Uzziel's son was Micah, and from Micah's descendants came Shamir.

decisions.choice: Shamir: the reading in the margin of the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew spells this name slightly differently; the copyists' marginal note reads Shamir, and that reading is followed. Micah is the son of Uzziel named in 23:20.

source.text: אֲחִ֤י מִיכָה֙ יִשִּׁיָּ֔ה לִבְנֵ֥י יִשִּׁיָּ֖ה זְכַרְיָֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] brother of Micah: Isshiah; to [the] sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.

en.L: The brother of Micah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
en.B: Micah's brother: Isshiah; from the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
en.R: Micah's brother was Isshiah, and from Isshiah's descendants came Zechariah.

decisions.choice: Isshiah: Uzziel's second son (23:20)
decisions.reason: This Isshiah of Uzziel's family is a different man from the Isshiah of Rehabiah's line in verse 21.

source.text: בְּנֵ֤י מְרָרִי֙ מַחְלִ֣י וּמוּשִׁ֔י בְּנֵ֖י יַעֲזִיָּ֥הֽוּ בְנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; [the] sons of Jaaziah, his son.

en.L: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; the sons of Jaaziah his son.
en.B: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; and the sons of Jaaziah, his son.
en.R: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Merari also had a son named Jaaziah, who had sons of his own.

decisions.choice: Jaaziah his son: Jaaziah was a son of Merari
decisions.reason: The last word can be read "his son", making Jaaziah a third son of Merari, whose sons follow in verse 27. It can also be read as a name, Beno, as the first of Jaaziah's sons. Jaaziah is not named elsewhere, so the list cannot be checked.

decisions.choice: Merari, Mahli and Mushi: as in 23:21
decisions.reason: The sons of Merari are the same as in 23:21 and Exodus 6:19.

decisions.choice: Merari also had a son named Jaaziah, who had sons of his own
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the reading chosen in m1, since "his son" would be unclear to young readers.

source.text: בְּנֵ֖י מְרָרִ֑י לְיַֽעֲזִיָּ֣הֽוּ בְנ֔וֹ וְשֹׁ֥הַם וְזַכּ֖וּר וְעִבְרִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Merari: by Jaaziah his son, and Shoham and Zaccur and Ibri.

en.L: The sons of Merari by Jaaziah his son: and Shoham and Zaccur and Ibri.
en.B: The descendants of Merari through his son Jaaziah: Shoham, Zaccur and Ibri.
en.R: Jaaziah's sons were Shoham, Zaccur and Ibri.

decisions.choice: by Jaaziah his son: Merari's descendants through Jaaziah
alternatives: of Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur and Ibri
decisions.reason: As in verse 26 (m1), the word is read "his son". The "and" before Shoham may show that a name has been lost before it, or that "Beno" is a name heading the list.

decisions.choice: descendants ... through; Jaaziah's sons
decisions.reason: Balanced says "descendants" because these are Merari's grandsons, and Readable names them as Jaaziah's sons.

source.text: לְמַחְלִי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֔ר וְלֹא־הָ֥יָה ל֖וֹ בָּנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: To Mahli: Eleazar, and not were to him sons.

en.L: Of Mahli: Eleazar, and he had no sons.
en.B: From Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.
en.R: Mahli's son was Eleazar, who had no sons.

decisions.choice: Eleazar had no sons
decisions.reason: 23:22 adds that Eleazar had only daughters, who married their cousins, the sons of Kish. This Eleazar is a Levite of Merari's family, not Aaron's son.

source.text: לְקִ֖ישׁ בְּנֵי־קִ֥ישׁ יְרַחְמְאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: To Kish: [the] sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.

en.L: Of Kish: the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.
en.B: From Kish: the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.
en.R: From Kish's family came Jerahmeel.

decisions.choice: Kish: Mahli's second son (23:21)
decisions.reason: Kish is the brother of Eleazar named in 23:21-22, a Levite and not the father of Saul. Jerahmeel is named here for the first time.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֣י מוּשִׁ֔י מַחְלִ֥י וְעֵ֖דֶר וִירִימ֑וֹת אֵ֛לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י הַלְוִיִּ֖ם לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Mushi: Mahli and Eder and Jerimoth. These [were the] sons of the Levites by house of their fathers.

en.L: And the sons of Mushi: Mahli and Eder and Jerimoth. These [were] the sons of the Levites by their fathers' houses.
en.B: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder and Jerimoth. These were the descendants of the Levites by their ancestral families.
en.R: Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder and Jerimoth. These were the Levites, listed by their families.

decisions.choice: Mahli, Eder and Jerimoth: as in 23:23
decisions.reason: 23:23 gives the same three sons of Mushi, spelling the last name Jeremoth.

decisions.choice: a closing line for the Levite list
decisions.reason: "These were the sons of the Levites" closes the list that began in verse 20, as 23:24 closed the earlier one.

source.text: וַיַּפִּילוּ֩ גַם־הֵ֨ם גּוֹרָל֜וֹת לְעֻמַּ֣ת׀אֲחֵיהֶ֣ם בְּנֵֽי־אַהֲרֹ֗ן לִפְנֵ֨י דָוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְצָד֣וֹק וַאֲחִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְרָאשֵׁי֙ הָֽאָב֔וֹת לַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְלַלְוִיִּ֑ם אָב֣וֹת הָרֹ֔אשׁ לְעֻמַּ֖ת אָחִ֥יו הַקָּטָֽן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And cast also they lots just as their brothers [the] sons of Aaron before David the king and Zadok and Ahimelech and [the] heads of the fathers of the priests and of the Levites: fathers, the head just as his brother the younger.

en.L: And they also cast lots, just as their brothers the sons of Aaron, before David the king and Zadok and Ahimelech and the heads of the fathers' [houses] of the priests and of the Levites: fathers' [houses], the head just as his younger brother.
en.B: These also cast lots, just as their relatives the descendants of Aaron had done, in the presence of King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the priestly and Levite families. The ancestral family of the head was treated just like that of his younger brother.
en.R: They also drew lots, as their relatives the priests had done. King David, Zadok, Ahimelech and the leaders of the priestly and Levite families were there. The oldest brother's family had no advantage over the family of his youngest brother.

decisions.choice: the head just as his younger brother: no advantage for rank or age
decisions.reason: The head of a family and his younger brother stood on equal terms when the lots were cast. As with the priests (verse 5), the lot alone set the order, not seniority.

decisions.choice: just as the sons of Aaron: the same procedure as verses 5-6
decisions.reason: The Levites' lots were cast the same way and before the same witnesses as the priests' lots in verse 6.

decisions.choice: relatives; the descendants of Aaron (Balanced); the priests (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means fellow members of the tribe of Levi, so Balanced and Readable say "relatives". Readable names Aaron's descendants as "the priests", which is who they were.

decisions.choice: the oldest brother's family ... the family of his youngest brother
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of m1 in plain words.
